**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `675e99ad08537cd224c84279013a2c3b6eb5c741` — the merge of head `48cd3c9ddcadbe8e5d92f6956d7e13b4ae08188d` into base `579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 675e99ad08537cd224c84279013a2c3b6eb5c741 && git checkout 675e99ad08537cd224c84279013a2c3b6eb5c741
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e 48cd3c9ddcadbe8e5d92f6956d7e13b4ae08188d && git checkout -B drift-repro 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e && git merge --no-ff 48cd3c9ddcadbe8e5d92f6956d7e13b4ae08188d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48cd3c9ddcadbe8e5d92f6956d7e13b4ae08188d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-summary-message.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts

FIRST round on this PR. Read for this record: card #37635 (body, triage comment 7198755801, claim comment 7206277918), records 7196337094 and 7197635792 on PR #37582 (the source of the card's four items: N3, N4, N6, N7 there), PR #37731 (body, 7-file list, the net diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code in the live tree. The rest of the diff (three test files, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the pins are read below only to answer whether each change has one.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept sets: none moves.** No Zod schema, authorable key, route or config field is in the diff. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`: none moves.** The diff changes comment lines in two jsdoc blocks of `i18n-resolver.ts` (+6/−3). The key union of `scalarOverridesPackagedBase` stays at its five keys and no export or signature changes. Right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: none moves.** `milestoneTokenRe` and `milestoneTokenNames` are exported from the module `activity-summary-message.ts`, which the package index does not re-export (the package has the one `.` entry). `ActivitySummaryMessage` gains an optional `names`, and that type is not on the index either. `Clause-②: no` is right.
- **Persisted shape: one new optional member, additive.** A fired milestone's row now stores `names` (a string list) inside `sys_activity.metadata.summary_message`, on the `activityMilestone` code only. It is written in one place (the fired-milestone branch of `audit-writers.ts`) and by no other writer. Its size is the count of distinct tokens in the authored `summary` template, so it is bounded by metadata and never by record data; `metadata` is an unbounded text column. Named additive and non-breaking: right, for these readers:
  - the summary middleware reads it and strips the whole code for every caller that is not the system, so no API reader is served it;
  - the field redaction narrows `fieldChanges` codes only and leaves this one to the middleware;
  - the app activity door refuses `summary_message` on an app's entry;
  - the Console's `recordActivityFeed.ts` reads `fieldChanges` codes only;
  - a system-context read (an export) sees one more key inside a JSON blob that no spec schema describes;
  - a reader built from `main` ignores the key, and this reader takes a code without it, so a rolling deploy is safe both ways.
- **What a reader is served changes in three cases.**
  1. A row whose translation names a token the template gained after the row was written: the stored sentence, where `main` serves the translation with a gap. The card's item 1: right.
  2. A translation naming a token the authored template never held: the stored sentence for every row of that milestone, where `main` renders the token empty. The dev's call, answered in ③.
  3. A row written by `main` since #37582 (no `names`) whose template held a token that was empty at write time, and whose translation names it: the stored sentence, where `main` serves the translation with that token empty, which was correct. A needless fallback, answered in ③.
- **Gate verdicts.** The check-runs on the head: 58 `success`, 11 `skipped`, none failing. `Test UI (9/16)` and its `Test UI` roll-up each have one earlier attempt that concluded `failure` and a later attempt that concluded `success`; no `ui/` package depends on plugin-audit, and the spec change is comment lines. Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates), Lint and Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Test Core 10 of 10 are green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `37635-milestone-summary-token-names.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. plugin-audit publishes a bug fix with no protocol change, so patch is right. The spec publishes doc comments only (they ship in its type declarations), and `none` takes patch: right.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, and match ①. Right.
- `Skills-docs: none` is on the PR body. No page under `skills/` describes the stored code. See N2 for the one docs row that describes the reader.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from the PR body's "Small calls made here (no card)":

1. **Store the template's token names on the row.** Accepted. It is the card's own example, it is the smallest datum that answers the question (was this token in the template that fired?), and it is taken from the same string the stored sentence is rendered from (`milestoneTokenNames(milestone.template)` beside `renderMilestoneSummary(milestone.template, …)`), so the names always cover the stored tokens.
2. **A token only the translation names also keeps the stored sentence.** Accepted. The spec's contract for the slot is that the translated template "carries the same `{field}` tokens as the authored `summary`" (`translation.zod.ts`), so such a translation is outside it, and the row has no value for the token under either rule. One rule for both cases is simpler than two. Its cost is in N2.
3. **A row with no stored names composes only when every token of the translation has a value.** Accepted as a deviation. It is case 3 of ①: the reader cannot tell "empty when written" from "added later" on such a row, and the PR chooses never to show a gap. The rows it costs are those written between #37582 and this PR on builds of `main`; the #37582 changeset is still unreleased, so no released version wrote one.
4. **The cache key is (object, field, value), finer than the card's (object, field).** Accepted. The answer depends on the value, and the packaged base is cached one level up, per object.

Claim-comment flags (container S, `mode:thread`, the serial-overlap note) are the lane seat's. `open_questions`: none on the PR body or the card.

SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The writer derives `names` from the template string it already holds; the reader composes from rows the read already returned, the in-memory bundle and the registered definitions. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` — holds.** Both sentences now agree with the predicate's declared key union, which is exactly `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, `message`, `summary`: "three scalars" and "its two callers" are gone, and the five are named as an object's three, a validation rule's `message` and an activity milestone's `summary`. The `summary` section below them is still true of the feed reader at this head: it asks `scalarOverridesPackagedBase(packaged, 'summary', served?.summary)` with the packaged milestone of the pair as `base`, now once per milestone per read. The new token rule is the composer's and is no part of what the predicate answers, so the jsdoc rightly does not mention it. One imprecision remains, N1.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-summary-message.ts` — agrees.** Read sentence by sentence against the `names` jsdoc, the composer comment and the changeset:

- *The fallback rule, by row shape.*
  - A row written before #37582 carries no code and is served as stored.
  - A row with `names`: a token with a stored value renders it; a token listed in `names` with no stored value renders empty, which is what the stored sentence has there; any other token makes the composer answer `undefined`, and `localizeActivityRow` then leaves the stored sentence in place.
  - A row without `names`: any token missing from `tokens` answers `undefined`.
  - A token only the translation names: `undefined`.
  - A stored value whose text is empty still counts as stored (the test is on the entry, not its text).
- *Is a row ever composed with a gap?* No. A token renders empty only when `names` lists it and `tokens` does not, and the writer produces that pair only for a token of the fired template whose value was empty.
- *Does a translated sentence fall back needlessly?* In the two cases ③ accepts (flags 2 and 3), and in no other I could build. Tried: a translation that omits an authored token (composes), a template with no tokens (`names` is empty and a token-free translation composes), a repeated token (one entry), a milestone removed from the served object (composes from the bundle as on `main`), a composed text that is empty (the stored sentence stands).
- *Malformed `names`* (a string, a list with a non-string) reads as `null`, so the row is served as stored; a code without `names` still reads. Fail closed, as the other members do.
- *One grammar.* `milestoneTokenRe()` is defined once, here, and returns a fresh `/g` instance per call. The composer's literal is gone, and `audit-writers.ts` imports the function. No other spelling of the single-brace grammar is left in plugin-audit.
- *The caches.* `milestoneTemplates` and `packagedBases` are closures of one `readerSummaryLocale` call, and the middleware makes that call once per `find` or `findOne`, after the rows are back. Nothing is module-level, so neither map outlives a read or crosses a tenant, a locale or an i18n service. A throwing service caches `undefined` for the rest of that read only, which is the stored sentence. The D9.2a judgment is still asked through the one exported predicate, with the same arguments as on `main`.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` — agrees.** The local `milestoneTokenRe` is deleted and imported, so the read plan, the render and `names` all use the one pattern. `names` is every distinct token of the template that fired, interpolated or not, which is what the reader's rule needs. The stored `summary`, `tokens`, `type` and `metadata.kind` are byte-for-byte what `main` writes, and the writer adds no read.

**`Fixes #37635` is right.** All four items are delivered: the fallback (item 1), one exported pattern (item 2), the per-read cache (item 3), and both spec sentences plus the test-file header (item 4).

**Do the pins fail without each change?** The composer rule: yes, in the unit file (the red-first case and three more) and through the real writer, driver and middleware in the integration file. `names` validation: yes. The writer storing `names`: yes, by the integration file's exact-shape assertion. Two halves have no pin, N3 and N4.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, each left as it is or carried to a follow-up card (a fix in code or tests moves the head):

- N1 (nit) — both spec sentences say the union names the scalars the predicate's callers ask about. Two callers outside the spec ask more through a cast: `displayKeyOverridesPackagedBase` in `packages/objectql/src/registry-top-level.ts` (a field's `inlineHelpText` and `placeholder`, an option's `label`) and `sourceOf` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.ts` (a field's `inlineTitle` and `relatedListTitle`, a related list's `label`). The sentences are exact for the declared union and silent about those. The card did not ask for it; fold it into a later change to that file.
- N2 (nit, follow-up candidate) — after flag 2, a translation that names a token its authored template lacks (a typo, or a token removed from the template and left in the translation) is never served for any row, and nothing reports it: `@objectstack/lint` has no token-parity rule for `_milestones`, and the reader's row in `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` says a reader in that language reads the row composed from the template, with no mention of the stored-sentence fallback. A lint finding (translation tokens outside the authored template's) would turn the silent fallback into an authoring-time message.
- N3 (nit, for the lane seat's ACCEPT) — the property the design rests on, that `names` holds tokens that were NOT interpolated, has no pin through the writer. The only writer-level assertion is on the won row, where every token was interpolated, so `names` equals the keys of `tokens` there. A writer that stored the interpolated names only would pass every test and send each row with an empty token to its stored sentence. One integration row whose template token is empty at write time would pin it.
- N4 (nit, for the lane seat's ACCEPT) — the cache case is titled "answers each milestone once per read" and counts packaged-base reads only. It goes red without `packagedBases` and stays green without `milestoneTemplates`, so the per-milestone answer map is unpinned. In-memory work only.
- N5 (nit) — the `[#37524]` paragraph of the module header in `activity-summary-message.ts`, not in this diff, still gives two outcomes (a translated language reads the translated template, a language with no entry reads the stored sentence). The third, added here, is stated on `names` and in the composer comment only.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 48cd3c9ddc · card #37635 · area s2-ux · 2026-11-27T03:42Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37731` is CLEAN: 13 items read, none flagged. All 58 checks on this head succeeded and 11 were expected skips. `Test UI (9/16)` passed on its second attempt. The seat re-ran it once with the reason on record, in 7208798506. `mergeable_state` is clean. There are 7 files. Patch changesets cover plugin-audit and spec. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** It was owed for two jsdoc blocks in `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`. Record 7209186281 on this head is a PASS, `No must-fix, no should-fix`, with five nits. The seat adopts it.
  - The fallback holds for every row shape, and no row is composed with a hole.
  - `names` is a new, additive, optional list inside `sys_activity.metadata.summary_message`. It is bounded by the template's distinct tokens, and it is stripped for every non-system caller. No reader breaks on it.
  - The token grammar is now defined once.
  - The per-read cache is a closure of one read, so it holds nothing across reads, tenants or locales.
- **`Fixes #37635` is right.** All four items of the card are delivered. The dev's small calls are listed in the PR body.
- **Changeset read sentence by sentence.** It matches the diff.
- **Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs` on the final 7-file list: not governed, 215 changed lines. Tier S.
- **Follow-ups.** N1 to N5 go to #37793. The seat weighed N3 and N4, the two pin gaps, as the reviewer asked. Neither changes behaviour on this head, so they ride the follow-up card rather than hold the PR.

Tier: S. Landing: ready + auto-merge by this stroke.
